purpose: Teach: 炸裂/廃墟/米兵/不毛/飢餓/自決/滅亡/査察

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、戦時下に爆弾が炸裂した事件の記録を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you covered wartime bomb incidents in your paper, didn't you?
lines.style: Steady, genuinely curious. Warm teacher-voice. Careful enunciation of his name. Leaning in slightly with interest, not interrogation.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、戦災の廃墟の中の生活史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I focused on everyday life in the ruins after air raids.
lines.style: Straightforward, a touch self-aware. Quiet confidence without performance. Slight upward lift at the end, inviting her to the next question.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、戦時下に米兵が駐留した影響を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: You covered the impact of American soldiers stationed during wartime in your paper, didn't you?
lines.style: Thoughtful pause before speaking. Gentle but precise. Not testing him — genuinely recalling. The tone of someone checking notes against memory.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、不毛な政治論争の研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I examined the history of futile political disputes from that period.
lines.style: Direct, matter-of-fact. No apology in the delivery. Slight weight on 'futile.' Brief and clear, trusting she'll understand the shift.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 世界の飢餓問題を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: You covered world hunger issues in your paper, didn't you?
lines.style: Engaged, alert. This question lands with genuine energy. Warm but focused. Teacher recognizing a shift in scope, inviting him to explain the connection.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、武士の自決の歴史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I looked at the history of samurai self-determination and honor.
lines.style: Calm, unhurried. Accepting the apparent jump without defensiveness. Small breath before starting. The ease of someone who knows why the connections matter.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、文明の滅亡を巡る考古学を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you covered archaeology around the collapse of civilizations in your paper, didn't you?
lines.style: Reflective, almost wondering. Slower pace. A teacher piecing something together out loud. Genuine intellectual curiosity, not a trap.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、国際査察制度の歴史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I studied the history of international inspection systems and oversight.
lines.style: Steady close. No hedging. Slight finality on the last word. Composed, ready for wherever this leads next.
